unit.title: Data
unit.blurb: Reading and drawing bar charts, dot plots, waffle diagrams and pie charts, grouped frequency diagrams, line graphs and scatter graphs.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Represent and interpret categorical data in bar charts, dot plots, waffle diagrams and pie charts.

O2.t: Represent and interpret grouped data in frequency diagrams, and data that changes over time in line graphs; read scatter graphs.

sections.title: Bar charts, dot plots, waffle diagrams and pie charts

p: A **bar chart** uses bars to show how many are in each group. Always read the **scale** on the axis carefully.
A **dot plot** shows each value as a dot. A **waffle diagram** is a 10 × 10 grid: each square is **1%**. A **pie chart** shows each group as a slice of a circle.

lesson.t: Why a pie chart shows parts of a whole
p: The whole circle is all the data. A sector that is half the circle shows half the data, whatever the total is.

lesson.q: 40 children chose a sport. A quarter of the pie chart is football. How many chose football?

p: Read the title, key and scale.
For a pie chart, use fractions of the circle.
If the scale goes up in 2s, a bar halfway between 8 and 10 shows 9.

q.prompt: In the bar chart, how many more children chose football than tennis?
Before you read on: which chart is best for showing the parts of one whole?

options.fb: Correct.
Dot plots show how often each value appears.
Line graphs show change over time.

sections.title: Frequency diagrams, line graphs and scatter graphs

p: A **frequency diagram** shows grouped data, such as heights 120–129 cm, 130–139 cm. The bars touch because the groups follow on from each other.
A **line graph** shows how something changes over time, such as temperature through a day.
A **scatter graph** plots pairs of values. If the points go up from left to right, as one value increases the other tends to increase.
Each point shows two measurements for one thing. If the points slope upwards, both measurements tend to increase together.

lesson.q: On a scatter graph of height and shoe size the points slope upwards. What does this show?
steps: as one increases, so does the other
lesson.a: Taller children tend to have bigger feet

p: Read both axes and their scales.
Use a ruler to read across from a point to the axis.

Before you read on: which graph shows how a temperature changes during a day?

Scatter graphs compare two measurements.
Pie charts show parts of a whole.

req.model: Height is measured data that is grouped. Each group follows straight on from the one before, with no gaps, so the bars touch.
req.reason: Height is measured data that is grouped. Each group follows straight on from the one before, with no gaps, so the bars touch.
